cards.explanation: The answer is the things above. Paul says to "…strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God." Notice the target is the things above, with Christ right there. It isn't a goal you'd put on a poster. I think that's a great thing to aim at, friends.

The answer is Christ. Paul writes, "For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God." Hidden with Christ, tucked in God like a batch tucked in the oven. That's a lot packed into one sentence.

The answer is that they appear with Him in glory. Paul says, "When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory." Christ IS their life, so when He appears, they appear right along with Him. Nobody gets left in the back of the line. This is one of the reasons my ovens stay ready.

The answer is True. Paul lists "sexual immorality, impurity, lust, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry." He puts greed in the same sentence as idolatry. That's a heavy list, and I think Paul meant for greed not to hide in it.

The answer is False. Paul says "…you also used to walk in these ways." The Colossians had lived among the people he just described. The key words there are "used to." That was their past, and verse 8 starts with "But now."

The answer is anger and slander. Paul's list says, "anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips." Anger and slander are both right there. That list is all about what comes out of us and how we treat each other, friends.

The answer is new. Paul says they "…have put on the new self…" Off with the old, on with the new. And he adds that this new self "…is being renewed…" so it's still being worked on. I can relate, because I got renewed once and I'm still getting the hang of it.

The answer is its Creator. Paul says the new self "…is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator." So the pattern isn't a person down here. It's the One who made it. That's the best blueprint a baker could ask for.

The answer is False. Paul says, "Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free, but Christ is all and is in all." He runs through the whole list and none of those lines stands. And the verse ends on Christ being all and in all, which is the best part.

The answer is compassion and kindness. Paul says to clothe yourselves "…with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience." Compassion and kindness are right at the front of that outfit. That's quite a wardrobe, friends. And the best part is, it's meant for the elect of God, holy and beloved.

The answer is False. Paul tells them to "…forgive any complaint you may have against someone else." He doesn't add a condition. Then he gives the measure: "Forgive as the Lord forgave you." Any complaint, friends, so no leftovers.

The answer is love. Paul says, "And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity." Love goes on over everything else, like the last layer before you head out the door. And it's the bond that holds it all together. Even a mustache needs wax, friends, and this outfit needs love.

The answer is that they were called to it as one body. Paul says, "Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body." The reason is their calling, and they were called together. One body means nobody is baking alone, friends. And then comes that short line: "And be thankful."

The answer is True. Paul says, "Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom…" The word dwells in them, and it spills out as they teach and admonish each other. Admonish is a word for warning and advising.

The answer is to do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus. Paul says, "…whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus…" Word or deed, everything goes under His name. It's a very big net. I'm glad it covers a batch of burnt cookies too.

The answer is True. Paul ends the verse with, "…giving thanks to God the Father through Him." The thanks goes to God the Father, and it goes through the Lord Jesus. Thankfulness shows up again and again in this passage, friends.
